full_judgment:
2. All the writ petitions have been filed challenging the judgment and decree of the Land Survey Tribunal of different districts passed in the respective land survey suits. Although section 145B of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act ("SAT Act") incorporates provisions for challenging judgment and decree of the Land Survey Tribunal by preferring appeal before the Land Survey Appellate Tribunal but at the relevant time of passing those decrees, there was no appellate forum due to which the petitioners of the respective writ petitions being aggrieved by the impugned judgment and decree, filed these writ petitions and obtained the Rules Nisi. 

 6. Section 145B of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 (hereinafter referred to as "the SAT Act") incorporates the provisions regarding appeal against the judgment and decree or order of the Land Survey Tribunal. The same are as follows: 

 "145B. Land Survey Appellate Tribunal—(1) The Government may, by notification in the official Gazette, establish as many Land Survey Appellate Tribunals as may be required to hear the appeals arising out of the judgment, decree or order of the Land Survey Tribunals. 

 (2) The Government may, by notification in the official Gazette, fix and alter the territorial limits of the jurisdiction of any Land Survey Appellate Tribunal. 

 [(3) The Government shall appoint the judge of the Land Survey Appellate Tribunal from among the persons who are District judges.] 

 [(3A) Until such judge is appointed under sub-section (3), the Government may empower the District Judge as the judge of the Land Survey Appellate Tribunal of the district. 

 (3B) The District Judge, empowered under sub-section (3A), shall be deemed to be the judge of the Land Survey Appellate Tribunal appointed under sub-section (3). (3C) The Government may, if necessary, appoint one or more Additional District Judges as a judge of the Land Survey Appellate Tribunal to hear appeals transferred by the judge of the Land Survey Appellate Tribunal appointed or empowered under this section.] 

 (4) No appeal other than the appeals arising out of the judgment, decree or order of the Land Survey Tribunal shall lie in the Land Survey Appellate Tribunal. 

 (6), any person aggrieved by any judgment, decree or order of the Land Survey Tribunal may, within three months from the date of such judgment, decree or order, prefer an appeal to the Land Survey Appellate Tribunal. (6) An appeal may be admitted within next three months even after the expiry of the period specified in sub-section (5), if the Land Survey Appellate Tribunal is satisfied with the reasons for delay shown by the appellant" 

 7. Upon perusal of the aforesaid provisions, it appears that sub-section (5) provides three months time to prefer appeal to the Land Survey Appellate Tribunal from the date of such impugned judgment and decree or order to be passed by the Land Survey Tribunal. Sub-section (6) provides further three months time, if the Land Survey Appellate Tribunal is satisfied with the reasons for delay shown by the appellant. 

 11. From the facts, it appears that although at the time of enactment of section 145B of the SAT Act in 2004, the Statute incorporated the provisions for preferring appeal within 3 months from the date of decree or order but the forum of appeal for the first time established by the State Acquisition and Tenancy (Amendment) Act, 2023 Gazetted on 7-6-2023 and by the Gazette Notification dated 23-8-2023, the jurisdiction of Land Survey Appellate Tribunal has been determined under different districts. In the circumstances, since the appellate forum has been established on 23-8-2023, we are of the view that the petitioners can take their grievances to the respective Land Survey Appellate Tribunals by preferring appeal challenging the impugned judgment and decree or order. 

 15. Limitation question in preferring appeal before the Land Survey Appellate Tribunal, has not yet been raised before the Appellate Division. However, at the time of disposing of two writ petitions arising out of decree of Land Survey Tribunal, the High Court Division passed an interim order of statusquo and it was adjudicated before the Appellate Division. Their lordships in passing the order on 15-10-2023 in Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal Nos. 1548 of 2023 and 1398 of 2023 held as under: 

 "We have heard the learned Counsel appearing for the petitioner in both the cases and perused the impugned judgment and orders of the High Court Division as well as other materials on record. Upon perusal it appears that section 145B of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 stipulates 3 (three) months' time for preferring appeal before the Land Survey Appellate Tribunal. 

 "Meanwhile status quo in respect of possession of the suit land shall continue till 3 (three) months from the date of establishment of the Land Survey Appellate Tribunal or from the date of empowering the District Judge as the Judge of the concerned Land Survey Appellate Tribunal under. section 145B(3A) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 (as amended in 2023)" 

 16. From the above order, it is apparent that due to non existence of the Land Survey Appellate Tribunal, the Apex Court extended the force of order of statusquo till 3 (three) months from the date of establishment of the said Appellate Tribunal. But here in these matters, 3 months limitation period have already been passed from the date of establishment of appellate forum. Yet on identical circumstances, we consider that due to non existence of Land Survey Appellate Tribunal, the writ petitioners could not challenge the impugned judgment and decree or order and this situation led them to file writ petitions obtaining Rules Nisi in their respective writ petitions. Thus, they have remained under the litigations before this Court so long. 

 22. Considering all these aspects and regard being had to the above, we are not inclined to dispose of the writ petitions on merit. Rather, we are of the view that the writ petitions shall be disposed of giving a liberty to the petitioners to prefer appeal before their respective appellate jurisdiction to testify the impugned judgment and decree or order of the Land Survey Tribunal. 

 (i) The petitioners are at liberty to prefer appeal before the respective Land Survey Appellate Tribunals with an application for condonation of delay and, if so filed, the respective Appellate Tribunal shall consider the application as well as the appeal in accordance with section 14 read with section 29 of the Limitation Act. (ii) Send down the lower Court's records in respect of writ petitions where the same have arrived in the meantime.
